$comment: Chapter spine for the cosmic clock, curated by lane R5 from the corpus spine files on 2026-09-06.

chapters.title: A hymn asks a question
chapters.line: Long before gods existed, one Vedic hymn wonders whether anyone, even a god, truly knows how the universe began.

chapters.title: The Self alone at first
chapters.line: The Upanishads say there was only one Self in the beginning, lonely, who became many so it would not be alone.

chapters.title: Brahma's lotus birth
chapters.line: Vishnu sleeps on the cosmic ocean and a lotus grows from his navel; Brahma sits on it and starts to build the worlds.

source.heading: III. Vaishnava Account — Brahma from the Lotus from Vishnu's Navel

chapters.title: Creation hatches from an egg
chapters.line: A golden egg floats on the first waters for a year, then splits open: its two halves become the sky and the earth.

art.alt: Dark water without a shore, lit only from within — the deep before anything has been raised out of it.

chapters.title: Shiva is the ultimate source
chapters.line: Shaiva texts say Shiva alone creates, keeps and destroys everything, and Brahma and Vishnu act only as his agents.

source.heading: V. Shaiva Account — Shiva / Sadashiva as Source

chapters.title: The Goddess makes the makers
chapters.line: In Shakta texts the Goddess is the ultimate power; without her, Shiva cannot even act, and she brings the Trimurti to life.

source.heading: VI. Shakta Account — Devi / Shakti as Primordial

art.alt: Light drawn out of many faces and gathered into one standing column of fire.

chapters.title: Creation unfolds in nine stages
chapters.line: The Puranas describe creation as an ordered sequence: mind, ego, the elements, plants, animals, gods, humans, and the ageless Kumaras.

source.heading: VII. Puranic Sequential Creation — Sarga & the Categories of Creation

chapters.title: Brahma populates the worlds
chapters.line: Brahma creates sons from his mind, then splits into the first man and woman, starting the family lines every later story rests on.

source.heading: VIII. Secondary Creation — Brahma's Mind-Born Sons, Rudra, and the Prajapatis

art.alt: The creator seated in a lit pavilion with figures gathered below: a court at the beginning of things.

chapters.title: Every story reaches one clock
chapters.line: However creation began, every tradition agrees Brahma now runs the current cycle, and his day is what starts the clock of ages.

source.heading: IX. Synthesis — How the Variants Relate

chapters.title: Svayambhuva, the first Manu
chapters.line: The first ruler of humankind and his wife begin the human family; their descendant Dhruva becomes the still Pole Star.

chapters.title: Svarochisha, born self-radiant
chapters.line: A romance between a sage and a nymph, tangled by a trickster's disguise, produces the glowing second ruler of the age.

source.heading: The Origin Legend — Svarocis and the Birth of Svārociṣa (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)

chapters.title: Uttama, the sparse record
chapters.line: The third age has almost no surviving story of its own, only a bare list of who ruled and who kept the sacred fires.

chapters.title: Tamasa and the trapped elephant
chapters.line: This age is remembered for Gajendra, an elephant-king seized by a crocodile, whose final cry brings Vishnu running to save him.

chapters.title: Raivata and a warped afternoon
chapters.line: A king waits what feels like a short while in Brahma's court, but millions of years pass on earth before he goes home.

chapters.title: Chakshusha, the age before ours
chapters.line: The final age before our own gathers stories the texts leave loosely dated: sages born of Anasuya, Shiva burning desire to ash, and the long life of King Yayati.

source.heading: Events, Stories & Figures of the Cākṣuṣa Age

chapters.title: Matsya saves the world
chapters.line: Vishnu becomes a fish, warns Manu of a coming flood, and tows his boat of survivors and seeds to safety.

chapters.title: Churning the ocean of milk
chapters.line: Devas and asuras team up to churn the ocean of milk for the nectar of immortality, and wonders and poison both rise up.

source.heading: ### Kūrma (the Tortoise) — Samudra Manthana (Churning of the Ocean of Milk)

chapters.title: Varaha lifts the earth
chapters.line: A demon drags the earth to the bottom of the ocean, so Vishnu becomes a giant boar, dives in, and carries her back up.

source.heading: ### Varāha (the Boar) — Hiraṇyākṣa & the lifting of the Earth

chapters.title: Narasimha bursts from a pillar
chapters.line: A tyrant cannot be killed by man or beast, day or night, indoors or out — so Vishnu becomes a man-lion and kills him at twilight on a doorstep.

chapters.title: Dhruva becomes the Pole Star
chapters.line: A boy pushed off his father's lap performs such fierce penance that Vishnu fixes him in the sky as the star everything turns around.

source.heading: ### Dhruva — the boy who became the Pole Star

art.alt: A small figure holding absolutely still by a cold lake while the sky presses down.

chapters.title: Daksha insults Shiva and Sati
chapters.line: A king snubs his own daughter and her husband Shiva at a great sacrifice; she burns herself alive, and Shiva's grief wrecks the ritual.

chapters.title: Two royal families begin
chapters.line: Manu's ten sons found the Solar dynasty of Ikshvaku and the Lunar dynasty, the two family lines every king in the epics belongs to.

source.heading: ### The founding of the royal lineages

art.alt: A king standing waist-deep in a river at first light, the water carrying everything downstream.

chapters.title: The first sages and seekers
chapters.line: The eternal child-sages, the teacher Kapila, and the twin ascetics Nara-Narayana all begin their long watch over dharma in this age.

source.heading: ### Early sages, mind-born sons & other Satya-Yuga origins

art.alt: A cavern under the earth, a seated ascetic, and a stillness that has clearly lasted a very long time.

chapters.title: Vamana tricks King Bali
chapters.line: Vishnu becomes a dwarf, asks a proud king for three paces of land, then grows to cover earth and sky and gently sets him underground.

chapters.title: Parashurama the warrior sage
chapters.line: A sage's son takes up an axe to punish kings who wronged his family, then waits immortal through every age since.

chapters.title: Ganga comes down to earth
chapters.line: A king does immense penance so the heavenly river Ganga will fall to earth and free his ancestors' ashes, and Shiva breaks her fall.

chapters.title: Rama is born and married
chapters.line: Prince Rama is born in Ayodhya, trains with a sage, breaks Shiva's great bow, and wins Sita's hand in Mithila.

art.alt: Brick and timber courts under an open sky, cultivated ground running away behind them.

chapters.title: Rama is exiled fourteen years
chapters.line: A stepmother's old promise sends Rama into the forest for fourteen years, and his father dies of grief at the parting.

art.alt: A dim hall of carved wooden posts with low seating and an empty seat at the far end.

chapters.title: Ravana steals Sita away
chapters.line: In the forest a demon king disguises himself as a beggar and carries off Rama's wife Sita to his island kingdom of Lanka.

art.alt: A forest floor in failing light, one figure down on a knee among the leaf litter.

chapters.title: Rama allies with the monkeys
chapters.line: Rama befriends the monkey prince Sugriva and the devoted Hanuman, who set out with an army to search for Sita.

chapters.title: Hanuman leaps across the sea
chapters.line: Hanuman leaps the ocean alone, finds Sita in captivity, gives her Rama's ring, and burns part of Lanka before flying home.

art.alt: Two figures meeting on an open shore at dusk, a camp of many others behind them.

chapters.title: The war for Lanka
chapters.line: Rama's army builds a bridge to Lanka, and after a huge battle Rama kills Ravana and brings Sita home to be crowned king.

art.alt: An island seen from very far off: dark headlands, a gold-lit citadel, sea on every side.

chapters.title: Rama's difficult homecoming
chapters.line: Gossip about Sita's time in captivity leads Rama to send her away; years later he learns of their twin sons and Sita returns to the earth.

chapters.title: The Kuru cousins are born
chapters.line: Vyasa fathers the blind Dhritarashtra and pale Pandu; their sons the Kauravas and Pandavas grow up rivals from the start.

source.heading: ## 2. The Kuru Lineage — Setup for the Mahābhārata

chapters.title: Krishna is born in prison
chapters.line: A tyrant king is warned his sister's eighth child will kill him, but that child is smuggled across a flooding river to safety.

chapters.title: Krishna grows up in Vrindavan
chapters.line: The cowherd boy Krishna dances on a poisonous serpent, lifts a whole mountain on his finger, and delights every child in the village.

chapters.title: Krishna kills Kamsa, builds Dvaraka
chapters.line: Grown up, Krishna kills the tyrant Kamsa, then leads his people to a new sea-fortress city called Dvaraka.

source.heading: ### Mathura, Kamsa & the move to Dvārakā

chapters.title: Balarama, Krishna's elder brother
chapters.line: Krishna's brother Balarama, who carries a plough as his weapon, teaches both cousins to fight and stays neutral in their war.

art.alt: Green riverbank pasture in flat morning light, cattle and two small figures far off.

chapters.title: The cousins become rivals
chapters.line: The Pandavas escape a burning palace, Arjuna wins Draupadi at her contest, and the cousins split the kingdom, sowing the seeds of war.

chapters.title: Draupadi's humiliation and exile
chapters.line: Yudhishthira gambles away everything, even Draupadi, in a rigged dice game, and the five brothers spend thirteen years in exile.

chapters.title: Krishna teaches the Bhagavad Gita
chapters.line: As the armies face off, Arjuna despairs at fighting his own family, and Krishna teaches him the Bhagavad Gita on the battlefield.

chapters.title: The eighteen-day war
chapters.line: Over eighteen days at Kurukshetra, teachers, brothers and sons fall one after another until almost no one is left standing.

chapters.title: Krishna departs, the age ends
chapters.line: Years after the war a curse destroys Krishna's clan, a hunter's arrow ends his life, and the sea swallows the city of Dvaraka.

source.heading: ## 6. The Close of Dvāpara — Yādava Destruction & Krishna's Departure

chapters.title: Kali Yuga begins at midnight
chapters.line: The last and shortest age begins the moment Krishna leaves the earth, traditionally dated to 3102 BCE, and lasts 432,000 years.

source.heading: ## 1. The Frame — When, How Long, How Reckoned

chapters.title: Dharma stands on one leg
chapters.line: The texts predict a world where wealth decides worth, rulers become predators, and only a quarter of virtue remains standing.

chapters.title: The prophesied kings of Kali
chapters.line: The Puranas list dynasty after dynasty that will rule after the Mahabharata war, right down to a king who erases caste entirely.

source.heading: ## 3. The Kali Yuga Kings — Puranic Dynasty Prophecy

chapters.title: Kalki, the final avatar
chapters.line: When wickedness peaks, Vishnu will come once more as the warrior Kalki, riding a white horse, to clear the world for a new age.

source.heading: ## 4. The End of Kali — Kalki, the Tenth Avatar

chapters.title: The wheel keeps turning
chapters.line: The end of Kali is not the end of the world, only the end of one cycle; a new Satya Yuga begins right after within the same great age.

chapters.title: Cities on the Indus
chapters.line: Planned cities rise along the Indus river with standardized weights and an undeciphered script, long before written history names a single king.

chapters.title: The Vedas take shape
chapters.line: Hymns to Agni, Indra and the other gods are composed and passed down by memory, later joined by the philosophical Upanishads.

source.heading: ## II. Vedic period (the śruti is composed)

chapters.title: Sixteen kingdoms and new teachers
chapters.line: Sixteen kingdoms rise across the land as cities and coins spread, and the Buddha and Mahavira challenge Vedic ritual; the great epics take their first shape.

source.heading: ## III. Second urbanization, Mahajanapadas & the śramaṇa challenge

chapters.title: Empires and the classical age
chapters.line: The Maurya and Gupta empires unite much of India, Ashoka rules from the throne, and the great Puranas are written down.

source.heading: ## IV. Empires & the consolidation of classical Hinduism

chapters.title: Temples rise, poet-saints sing
chapters.line: Great temple-building dynasties raise stone monuments in the south, while poet-saints sing devotional hymns to Vishnu and Shiva in Tamil.

source.heading: ## V. Classical temple & dynasty era; the rise of devotional South India

art.alt: A mountain path at dawn crowded with people walking upward, lamps and cloth against grey rock.

chapters.title: The great philosopher-teachers
chapters.line: Shankara, Ramanuja and Madhva each found their own school of Vedanta, arguing over how the soul and God are related.

source.heading: ## VI. The Acharyas (Vedanta founders) — note the traditional/scholarly date gap

chapters.title: Poet-saints of devotion
chapters.line: Kabir, Mirabai, Tulsidas and Guru Nanak spread passionate devotion to God in everyday language across northern India.

source.heading: ## VII. The Bhakti & Sant movement (north India, 14th–17th c.)

chapters.title: Empires, gurus and Shivaji
chapters.line: Mughal rulers alternately patronize and destroy temples while Shivaji builds a Hindu kingdom in the west and the Sikh Gurus lead in the north.

chapters.title: Reformers and a Hindu renaissance
chapters.line: Ram Mohan Roy, Dayananda Saraswati and Vivekananda reshape Hindu thought for the modern world and carry it to a world stage in Chicago.

source.heading: ## IX. Colonial-era reform & the "Hindu Renaissance" (19th–early 20th c.)

chapters.title: Hinduism in the modern world
chapters.line: Gandhi reinterprets the Gita as a call to nonviolence, and gurus carry yoga and Vedanta to a global audience through the twentieth century.

chapters.title: Kalki clears the way
chapters.line: Once Kalki has destroyed the wicked, the minds of everyone left turn naturally pure, and they become the first people of the next golden age.

source.heading: The dawn of the new age

chapters.title: Only the end of Kali
chapters.line: Finishing this Kali Yuga only completes one quarter-turn of the wheel: forty-three more Mahayugas remain before this Manvantara itself is done.

chapters.title: Seven Manus still to come
chapters.line: After ours, seven more Manus will each rule their own long age, the last of them named Indra-savarni, before this Day of Brahma ends.

chapters.title: The Night of Brahma falls
chapters.line: When all fourteen Manus have ruled, fire and flood destroy the lower worlds and Brahma sleeps through a night as long as his day.

chapters.title: The next dawn always comes
chapters.line: Even after Brahma's whole hundred-year life ends in total dissolution, tradition holds that time is beginningless and endless, and a new Brahma always follows.

chapters.title: The doorkeepers' three lives
chapters.line: Two gatekeepers of heaven choose three quick lives as Vishnu's enemies over seven slow ones as devotees, and each life forces him to descend.

source.heading: ## The three births — one curse across three yugas

chapters.title: The gods create Durga
chapters.line: When a buffalo-demon defeats every god, they pour their light together into one being: the goddess Durga, who alone can stop him.

chapters.title: Kali licks up every drop
chapters.line: A demon who multiplies from every drop of his own spilled blood is finally stopped when Kali licks up each drop before it touches ground.

chapters.title: Shiva burns desire to ash
chapters.line: The gods send Kama, god of desire, to wake grieving Shiva's love for Parvati; Shiva burns him to ash with a glance, then relents.

source.heading: ### The burning of Kāma and his rebirth as Pradyumna

chapters.title: The brothers race the world
chapters.line: Ganesha and Kartikeya compete to see who can circle the world first; Ganesha wins by simply walking around his own parents.

source.heading: ### The race around the parents (vs Kārtikeya)

chapters.title: The boy who outlived time
chapters.line: Granted a short but limitless life, the sage Markandeya survives the dissolution of the entire universe and sees the infant form of God floating on the flood.

source.heading: ## 4. The Pralaya Vision — Bāla-Mukunda on the banyan leaf

chapters.title: Savitri argues with Death
chapters.line: When Death comes to take her husband, Savitri follows him on foot, out-argues him with clever boons, and wins her husband's life back.

source.heading: ## The dialectical duel — the five boons

chapters.title: Gods and demons at war
chapters.line: One Purana counts twelve separate wars between gods and demons, a rivalry so constant the texts treat it as the engine of history itself.

source.heading: ## The Twelve Wars, one by one

art.alt: A fortress of gold riding in an empty sky — power built to be unreachable.
